CHAPTER 864
Sidewalk and Street Sales
864.01   Conducting business in public way; permit required; effective period.
864.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES  
   Sidewalk obstructions, damage or injury - see GEN. OFF.
660.10
   License and permit issuance and revocation - see B. R. & T.
Ch. 804 
   Misrepresenting quality or price - see B. R. & T.
808.05
864.01 CONDUCTING BUSINESS IN PUBLIC WAY; PERMIT REQUIRED; EFFECTIVE PERIOD.
   (a)   No person shall use any sidewalk, street or alley in the City for the
purpose of selling, displaying or exhibiting any goods, wares, merchandise,
real estate, food and drink or livestock, except;
      (1)   When such sale is conducted pursuant to an order of a court;
      (2)   When authority is granted by the Director of Public Service, which
authority shall be evidenced by a permit allowing the sale of such merchandise
upon sidewalks, streets or alleys to be specified in such permit. The Director
shall issue such a permit only when the applicants have satisfactorily
demonstrated that the permit is to be used in connection with a cooperative
effort on the part of local merchants to promote business, and the permit shall
be issued to not fewer than ten of such merchants or to an organization
representing not fewer than ten of such merchants.
      (3)   When authority is granted by the Director to a food service
establishment for the purpose of operating a sidewalk cafe or similar outdoor
eating facility upon a sidewalk in a manner to be specified in such permit. The
Director shall issue such a permit only when the applicant has satisfactorily
demonstrated that the operation of the sidewalk cafe or similar eating facility
is in conjunction with and contiguous to a regular food service establishment
owned or operated by the applicant. No permit shall be issued by the Director
until the applicant has presented to the Director a certificate from the City
Board of Health, or its authorized representative, indicating that the sale of
food and beverage, in the manner contemplated, is permissible and that the
operation of the sidewalk cafe or similar facility is covered by all necessary
licenses and permits issued by the Board of Health to the applicant for the
operation of such a facility, notwithstanding any other provision of this
chapter.
      (4)   When business establishments regularly occupying structures in the
General Business District, as shown on the Zoning Map of the City, as from time
to time amended, conduct sales on sidewalks immediately adjacent to the
structure occupied by the business establishment that are ten-feet wide or
more, provided that the sale is not conducted in such a manner as to interrupt
the flow of sidewalk pedestrian traffic or to otherwise constitute a nuisance
or hazard. Such sales may be conducted without the necessity of first obtaining
a permit. Signs not in conflict with the sign ordinance and promotional robots
which advertise sales and special events may be placed upon the sidewalk,
provided that those items do not interrupt the flow of sidewalk pedestrian
traffic or otherwise constitute a nuisance or hazard.
   (b)   No person shall use any sidewalk, street or alley in the City, even
though such person may have received a permit issued pursuant to this chapter,
if the Director of Public Service determines that the use of such sidewalk,
street or alley constitutes a hazard or an impediment to persons wishing to use
such sidewalk, street or alley for passage. No person, after having been
notified by the Director or his or her authorized agent to cease and desist
such operation or use of a sidewalk, sheet or alley, or to otherwise modify
such operation or use, shall continue to use such sidewalk, street or alley in
contravention of such order or notice of the Director.
   (c)   Permits issued by the Director under paragraph (a)(2) hereof shall be
effective for not more than seven days. Permits issued by the Director under
paragraph (a)(3) hereof shall be effective from May 1 to August 31 of each
year.
(Ord. 89-70. Passed 11-6-89.)
864.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates section 864.01(a) is guilty of a minor misdemeanor
and shall be fined not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00) for the first
day of the violation. For each day thereafter, that a violation continues, such
person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined not
more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned not more than
thirty days, or both.
   (b)   Whoever violates Section
864.01(b) is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined
not more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250® 00) or imprisoned not more than
thirty days, or both, for the first day of the violation. For each day
thereafter, that a violation continues, such person is guilty of a misdemeanor
of the third degree and shall be fined not more than five hundred dollars
($500. 00) or imprisoned not more than sixty days, or both.
(Ord. 83-20. Passed 4-18-83. )

868.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Public swimming pool" means any structure, basin, chamber or tank
containing a body of water for swimming, diving or recreational bathing and
having a depth of two feet or more at any point, other than a private
residential swimming pool, intended to be used collectively by numbers of
persons for swimming or bathing, regardless of whether a fee is charged for
such use, and operated by any person, whether as owner, lessee, operator,
licensee or concessionaire.
   (b)   "Person" means any individual, firm, partnership, association,
corporation, company, governmental agency, club or organization of any kind.
   (c)   "Operator" means the person who is in responsible charge of operating
a swimming pool.
(Ord. 71-35.Passed 3-15-71. )
868.02 PERMIT REQUIRED; EXPIRATION.
   (a)   No person shall operate or maintain a public swimming pool without
first obtaining a permit therefor from the Board of Health. All permits issued
by the Board to operate a swimming pool shall expire on April 30 following the
date of issuance.
   (b)   Any person who, subsequent to May 1 of any year, proposes to operate a
public swimming pool during any remaining part of the year, shall apply for and
obtain a permit therefor from the Board not less than ten days before such
public swimming pool is to be opened.
(Ord. 71-35. Passed 3-15-71.)
868.03 PERMIT FEE.
   The permit fee for either permit required by Section
868.02 shall be twenty-five dollars ($25. 00) per year or any part of a year.
(Ord. 71-35. Passed 3-15-71. )
868.99 PENALTY.
   EDITOR'S NOTE: See Section
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.

872.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Taxicab" means all motor vehicles carrying passengers for hire on the
streets of the City except motor buses operated on regularly established routes
and except Senior Sedans, as provided for in
Chapter 1066 of Part Ten - the Streets, Utilities and Public Services Code.
Wherever the word "cab" is used in this chapter it shall be construed to mean a
motor vehicle subject to regulations by this chapter.
   (b)   "Taxicab owner" means every corporation, - association, joint stock
association, person, firm or partnership, their lessees, directors, receivers
or trustees, appointed by any court, or the personal representatives or assigns
of any deceased owner, owning, controlling, operating or managing any taxicab.
   (c)   "Taxicab driver" means the person driving a taxicab.
   (d)   "Taxicab revenue" means all moneys or the value of all user-subsidized
transportation tokens received by the driver from the operation of a taxicab.
   (e)   "Director" means the Director of Public Safety or his successor.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.02 POWERS AND DUTIES OF DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC SAFETY.
   The Director of Public Safety is hereby authorized to make such rules and
regulations governing the issuance of taxicab and taxicab driver's licenses or
any other matter under the Director of Public Safety's supervision and control
as are reasonable, necessary and not inconsistent with this chapter. The
Director of Public Safety may act upon, make findings upon and grant, deny,
suspend or revoke taxicab and taxicab driver's licenses as well as place
taxicab owner or driver on probation due to noncompliance with the licensing
regulations herein.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.03 TAXICAB LICENSE APPLICATION.
   Application for a taxicab license shall be made to the Director of Public
Safety upon blanks provided by him and shall set forth the name and address of
the applicant, the trade name under which he does business, the class of
vehicle for which the license is desired, the seating capacity and any other
relevant information required by the Director of Public Safety on said
application. If the application is granted, the applicant shall furnish the
Director, prior to the issuance of the license, information covering the
particular vehicle to be licensed, including the make and the State license
number of the vehicle, the length of time the vehicle has been in use, the
motor number and/or the serial number thereof.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.04 TAXICAB LICENSE FEES.
   No taxicab shall be operated in the City unless a license therefor has been
issued to the owner/lessee thereof and is in force. Every license shall expire
on December 31 of the year for which it is issued. If a license is issued for
operation on or after July 1 of any year, the fee shall be one-half of the
annual fee. The annual fee shall be twenty dollars ($20.00) per cab and shall
be in addition to the fee required for motor vehicle licenses under the laws of
the State of Ohio.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.05 TAXICAB LICENSE ISSUANCE.
   (a)   The Director of Public Safety shall investigate each applicant for a
taxicab license. The Director of Public Safety shall investigate and hold a
hearing as to each applicant for a license. If the Director of Public Safety
finds from such investigation and hearing, if said fearing is held, that the
provisions of this chapter and the Ohio Revised Code have been met, the
Director of Public Safety shall notify the applicant of the Director of Public
Safety's findings and the license shall be issued.
   (b)   If the Director of Public Safety finds that the applicant, at that
time, has not complied with this chapter, the Director of Public Safety may
require the applicant to furnish, within 30 days, any additional relevant
information required. If the Director of Public Safety then finds that the
applicant is the owner of the vehicle for which a license is desired, that such
vehicle is safe and fit for the public's conveyance and that the vehicle and
the applicant comply with this chapter and relevant portions of the Ohio
Revised Code, then the Director of Public Safety shall so notify the applicant,
and the Director of Public Safety shall issue a license to the applicant upon
the payment of the proper license fee.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.06 LIABILITY INSURANCE REQUIRED.
   No license to operate any taxicab shall be issued or renewed by the Director
of Public Safety until the owner of the same deposits and a policy of a
liability insurance policy issued by a company duly licensed to transact
business in the State of Ohio. The insurance policy shall insure, within the
amount specified in such policy, the owner of such taxicab and also any other
person (herein called the operator) operating the same in the City as a taxicab
under the authority of such owner, whether such authority is under contract of
employment, lease or other transaction between the owner or the owner's
assignee or lessee and such person operating such car, against loss from the
liability imposed by law for damages on account of bodily injury or death and/
or for damage to property (other than injury, death or property damage of the
insured or insured's employees) resulting from such ownership, maintenance or
use of such taxicab. The insurance policy shall also contain language
obligating the insurer to pay to any judgment creditor, to the extent of the
respective amounts specified in such policy, and to pay any final judgment
rendered against the insured or such operator by reason of such liability. In
addition thereto, such policy of insurance shall contain an endorsement
providing that the policy is in full force and effect and binding upon the
insurance company until the date specified for its expiration or until such
insurance company has given the Director 20 days notice in writing of such
company's intent to cancel such policy.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.07 EXTENT OF LIABILITY.
   The limit in any such insurance policy of the liability of the insurer on
account of the ownership, maintenance and use of each taxicab shall be not less
than one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) for bodily injury to or death of
one person and, subject to such limit as to the injury or death of one person,
three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) on account of any one accident
resulting in injury to and/or death of more than one person and fifty thousand
dollars ($50,000) on account of damage to property in any one accident.
(Ord. 87-60. Passed 12-21-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.08 CANCELLATION OF POLICY BY INSURER.
   Upon cancellation of the insurance policy, the insured shall provided 30
days notice to the Director of Public Safety. However, this provision shall not
be construed to waive any lawful notice which the insurer must give to the
insured. If a license is revoked for failure to maintain insurance, upon the
filing of a new insurance policy, the Director of Public Safety may reinstate
the license if a new insurance policy is provided within 45 days of revocation,
along with payment of a twenty dollar ($20.00) reinstatement fee.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.09 TAXICAB LICENSE REVOCATION.
   (a)   Nonpayment of Judgment. In the event of a final judgment or award by a
court of record against the owner of a taxicab, for damages on account of
bodily injury or death and/or for damage to property, if such judgment or award
is not paid within thirty days thereafter, the Director of Public Safety shall
forthwith revoke all licenses of all the taxicabs of such owner.
   (b)   Failure to Operate.
      (1)   Whenever any person holding one or more licenses for taxicabs fails
to make a reasonable and consistent effort to operate any such licensed
taxicab, for a period of 60 days, the Director of Public Safety shall notify
the holder of the license and the Director shall revoke the license for such
taxicab.
      (2)   However, any such person who desires to discontinue the services of
such taxicab or taxicabs for a short period of time, may do so for a period of
not less than 60 days or more than 120 days by so notifying the Director and
depositing with the Director the licenses for such taxicab or taxicabs.
However, if such taxicab or taxicabs so discontinued from service are not
placed in service at the expiration of such 120-day period, such license or
licenses therefor shall be revoked.
   (c)   Required Procedure. No revocation provided for in subsections (a) and
(b) hereof shall be effective until the procedures provided for in Section
804.02 have been complied with.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.10 TRANSFER OF LICENSE.
   (a)   Vehicle to Vehicle. In the event that the owner of a licensed taxicab
ceases to own the same or in the event that such vehicle becomes unsuitable for
operation, an affidavit to such effect may be filed with the Director of Public
Safety who shall thereupon transfer the license to any such vehicle belonging
to such owner, provided that such vehicle is approved by the Director of Public
Safety and this chapter and relevant provisions of the Ohio Revised Code have
been satisfied.
   (b)   Owner to Owner. No taxicab license shall be transferred from one owner
to another.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.11 IDENTIFICATION, PAINTING AND LETTERING.
   Every person owning and operating a taxicab under a license from the City
may adopt a trade name, design, color scheme or method of painting or lettering
such taxicab that is approved by the Director of Public Safety. Such trade
name, design, color scheme or method of painting or lettering shall meet the
following requirements:
   (a)   A serial body number may be painted on each side and on the rear of
the taxicab.
   (b)   The name of the owner or the trade name under which he does business
shall be painted on each side of each taxicab. Whenever the name of the owner
or trade name under which he does business does not include any of the words
“taxicab,” “taxi” or “cab,” then the word “taxicab” may be painted on each side
of the taxicab immediately beneath such name or trade name.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.12 TAXICAB REQUIREMENTS.
   (a)   Every taxicab shall be kept in a safe and sanitary operating condition
and shall at all times have all safety equipment required of taxicabs by the
Ohio Revised Code.
   (b)   Annual vehicle safety inspections will be conducted at the expense of
the owner or lessee by an entity or person certified to perform a safety
inspection. A copy of the inspection report will be forwarded to the office of
the Director of Public Safety prior to the original issue or renewal of the
taxicab license.
   (c)   Inspections shall include but not be limited to the following items:
brakes, windshield wipers, horn, rear-view mirror, windows, steering, tires,
mufflers, air conditioner, heater/defroster, seat belts, headlights,
taillights, back-up lights, flashers, dome light, license plate light, brake
light, turn signals, two-way radio, and the exterior/interior condition of the
vehicle.
   (d)   If any portion of the inspection is unsatisfactory, the owner/lessee
shall cause the condition to be corrected before the issuance of the license is
granted.
   (e)   The Director of Public Safety may make or cause additional inspections
of taxicabs during the 12-month period after a license is issued.
   (f)   If upon any such inspection, a taxicab is found to be unsafe, the
Director of Public Safety may direct the vehicle to be taken out of service
until the condition is corrected.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.13 CARRYING CAPACITY.
   No taixcab shall carry more passengers than such vehicle was designed to
carry.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.14 TAXICAB DRIVER'S LICENSE REQUIRED; APPLICATION.
   (a)   No person shall drive a taxicab unless duly licensed as hereinafter
provided.
   (b)   Every driver of a taxicab, before receiving such license, shall make
application to the Director of Public Safety on forms to be supplied by the
Director of Public Safety.
   (c)   The application form shall further contain the certificate of a
licensed physician who shall certify, after examination, that the applicant is
medically capable of driving a taxicab. The certificates by the physician shall
be renewed annually.
   (d)   The applicant shall file with his application an Ohio driver’s license
abstract for the preceding three years and two acceptable, close-up
photographs, two inches by three inches in size, which shall have been taken
within 30 days preceding the date of the application.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.15 TAXICAB DRIVER'S LICENSE FEES.
   Every driver of a taxicab, before receiving a taxicab driver's license,
shall pay to the Director of Public Safety a fee of ten dollars ($10.00) for
the first year and five dollars ($5.00) per year for renewals thereof.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.16 APPLICATION AND DISQUALIFICATIONS.
   (a)   After complying with relevant provisions of the application process,
each application shall be examined by the Director of Public Safety as to
whether or not the applicant has obtained relevant licensing from the State as
to the applicant's traffic and criminal record.
   (b)   If upon checking the record of any applicant for an original license
or for renewal of a license, the Director of Public Safety shall disqualify
from the issuance of a license if the applicant has been convicted within the
past five years or has charges pending for any of the following crimes: any
felony in which physical violence was used, traffic-related homicide,
manslaughter or assault, rape or any other sex offense, burglary, arson, any
felony drug offense, and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
   (c)   Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the discretion of
the Director of Public Safety to refuse to issue a license for other background
related issues.
   (d)   Applicants for an original license will submit to a BCI Background
Check at their expense and shall submit or cause the submission of the results
with their application.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 01-28. Passed 5-
21-01; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.17 TAXICAB DRIVER'S LICENSE ISSUANCE OR DENIAL.
   (a)   If the Director of Public Safety is satisfied that the applicant is a
suitable and proper person to drive a taxicab, and if the applicant's
examination discloses no matters which prevent the issuance or renewal of a
license, then the Director of Public Safety shall grant such license upon
receipt of the proper fee.
   (b)   It will be the responsibility of the owner/lessee of the taxicab
company to ensure that all drivers have the required city taxicab driver’s
license.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.18 DRIVER'S LICENSE RENEWAL.
   (a)   A taxicab driver's license shall expire on December 31 of each year.
An application for renewal of such license shall be filed with the Director of
Public Safety at least 30 days prior to the expiration date. Failure to comply
with this section will result in paying a penalty of ten additional dollars
($10.00) late renewal fee.
   (b)   Each renewal application form shall contain the certificate of a
licensed physician to whom the applicant has presented himself for examination,
which physician shall certify that the applicant is free from each infirmity
mentioned in Section 872.15(b) except that an examination for a communicable
social disease is not required in the case of a renewal application, unless in
the opinion of the Director it is believed to be desirable.
   (c)   The Director shall take action on each such application for a license
renewal prior to its expiration. In event of a refusal to renew a license, the
proceedings as to notification and appeal shall be the same as in cases where
an original application was denied.
   (d)   Original applications granted after November 1 and prior to the
renewal date will not require a medical examination or a police check for
renewal.
   (e)   Licenses issued on or after October 1 on original applications may be
used prior to January 1 without additional charge.
   (f)   Licenses issued on approved renewal applications on and after December
1 may be used at once.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-
16-12.)
872.19 CHANGE OF ADDRESS AND EMPLOYMENT.
   Every licensed driver shall have his residential address along with the
company with whom he or she works at the time of the issuance or renewal of the
license on file with the Director of Public Safety and, in the event of an
address change, shall notify the Director in person within seven days after
making such change. The driver shall present such driver's license for
correction.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.20 LICENSE REVOCATION OR SUSPENSION.
   (a)   Reasons. The Director of Public Safety, after notice and a hearing,
may permanently revoke or temporarily suspend the taxicab driver's license of
any licensed driver for any of the following reasons:
      (1)   The licensee has obtained a license by any false statement in his
application or has made any misrepresentation or false statement in his
affidavit in applying for a duplicate badge.
      (2)   The licensee has become physically or mentally incapable of driving
a taxicab.
      (3)   The licensee has been convicted of, or has pleaded guilty to, a
crime involving moral turpitude.
      (4)   The licensee has contracted and is suffering from a communicable
social disease, in which case his license shall be reinstated when satisfactory
proof is presented to the Director, by medical certificate, of complete
recovery.
   (b)   Notice. The Director of Public Safety shall notify the driver of any
hearing of the Director involving the suspension or revocation of a license and
shall require such driver to turn in his certificate, license and
identification card. Such notification shall be by registered or certified
mail, directed to the last address of the driver on file with the Director.
   (c)   Appeal. The Mayor shall hear appeals from the action of the Director
in matters of denial, suspension or revocation of licenses.
   A driver who has been refused a license or whose license has been denied,
suspended or revoked may, except where the denial, suspension or revocation is
mandatory, appeal to the Mayor within ten days after the date of mailing of the
notice of denial, suspension or revocation. The Mayor may consider such appeal
in whatever manner it may determine and its decision thereon shall be final.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.21 EMPLOYMENT OF UNLICENSED DRIVERS.
   No owner of any taxicab shall knowingly permit the same to be driven for
hire by anyone who is not licensed under this chapter. In the event that such
vehicle is so driven, the Director of Public Safety shall revoke the vehicle
license for the vehicle concerned and for all other vehicles owned by the same
owner.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.22 RECORDS.
   The owner or person in charge of one or more taxicabs shall keep a record of
all such taxicabs, showing the body number, the City license number and such
data as may be necessary to identify the driver of such vehicle or vehicles at
any and all times. Such record shall be subject to inspection at all times by
the public and shall not be destroyed for a period of six months.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.23 USE OF NONLICENSED VEHICLES.
   No person shall use any vehicle, other than a taxicab duly licensed under
and operating in accordance with the provisions of this chapter, for
transporting the public generally, as passengers for hire, reward, gift,
donation or other consideration. However, this section shall not apply to motor
buses or omnibuses operating under proper authority or to senior sedans.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.24 VEHICLES FROM OTHER CITIES.
   Taxicabs whose place of business is not in the City may bring passengers
into the City, but may not pick up any passenger from any destination or accept
any business in the City, except upon compliance with this chapter.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.25 FAILURE TO PAY FARE.
   No person shall engage any taxicab with intent to defraud the owner or
driver thereof. Refusal to pay the lawful charge for such vehicle or leaving
the same without payment or offer to pay shall be prima-facie evidence of such
intent to defraud.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.26 DEFACING CERTIFICATES.
   No licensed taxicab driver shall knowingly deface any license certificate,
tag or identification card issued pursuant to this chapter or remove, tamper
with or alter the same. In the case of a violation of this section, the
Director of Public Safety may revoke the violator's license. Such revocation
shall be in addition to the penalty provided in Section
872.99.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.27 OPERATION WITHOUT VEHICLE LICENSE.
   No person shall operate or permit to be operated for hire, reward, gift,
donation or other consideration, an unlicensed vehicle for transporting the
public generally as passengers. In the case of a violation of this section, the
violator shall not thereafter be granted a license for the vehicle concerned
for a period of three months for the first violation and one year for a
subsequent violation. Such remedy shall be in addition to the penalty provided
in Section
872.99.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.28 DRIVING WHILE DRIVER'S LICENSE SUSPENDED.
   No licensed taxicab driver shall drive a taxicab during a period of
suspension of his license. In the case of a violation of this section, it shall
be mandatory upon the Director of Public Safety to revoke the license of such
driver. Such driver shall not be eligible to receive a new license for a period
of one year from the date of such revocation.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.29 FARE RATE SCHEDULES.
   (a)   Every person owning and operating a taxicab under license from the
City shall file in the Office of Public Safety a complete schedule of fares and
rates charged passengers for transportation.
   (b)   Every person owning and operating a taxicab under license from the
City shall display at all times a printed rate card of the fares and rates to
be charged passengers for transportation. No operator shall charge a fare or
rate more than those so displayed.
(Ord. 00-31. Passed 9-5-00; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
872.99 PENALTY.
   (a)   Whoever violates or fails to comply with any of the provisions of this
chapter for which no other penalty is provided, is guilty of a minor
misdemeanor for a first offense and shall be fined not more than one hundred
dollars ($100.00); for a second offense or subsequent offense, such person is
guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree and shall be fined not more than
two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned not more than 30 days, or
both. A separate offense shall be deemed committed each day during or on which
such violation or noncompliance occurs or continues.
   (b)   Whoever violates Section
872.29 is guilty of a misdemeanor of the fourth degree on a first offense and
shall be fined not more than two hundred fifty dollars ($250.00) or imprisoned
not more than 30 days, or both. A separate offense shall be deemed committed
each day during or on which a violation occurs or continues.
(Ord. 87-56. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 12-11. Passed 4-16-12.)
CHAPTER 876
Temporary Stores
876.01   Definitions; presumption.
876.02   License required; fee.
876.03   Bond required.
876.04   Exceptions.
876.99   Penalty.
   CROSS REFERENCES  
   Power to regulate - see Ohio R. C. 715. 64
   Placing harmful substance or objects in food or confection - see GEN. OFF.
636.15
   Smoking prohibited in retail stores and elevators - see GEN. OFF.
660.13
   License and permit issuance and revocation - see B. R. & T.
Ch. 804 
   Signs over streets and sidewalks - see B. R. & T.
808.04
   Misrepresenting quality or price - see B. R. & T.
808.05
   Production and exhibition of weights, etc. for testing - see B. R. & T.
880.03
876.01 DEFINITIONS; PRESUMPTION.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "Temporary store" means a barbershop or beauty parlor or a store,
storeroom, office or other place opened and maintained for the sale to or
purchase from the public of goods, commodities or merchandise, and where the
operator or owner of such barbershop or beauty parlor or the seller, buyer or
owner of such goods, commodities or merchandise operates such store, storeroom,
office cr other place for a period of less than 120 days. Any store which is
opened, operated and maintained in the City shall prima-facie be presumed to be
a temporary store within the meaning of this chapter, but such presumption may
be overcome by evidence satisfactory to the Mayor that it is not a temporary
store as defined herein, in which case the Tax Commissioner shall not be
required to collect the license fee or take a bond in lieu of payment thereof,
as hereinafter provided.
(1969 Code Sec. 110.07)
   (b)   'Person" means any individual, association, partnership or
corporation, or the operator for or the agent of the same, who buys from or
sells to the public at retail, through or by means of such temporary stone, any
goods, commodities or merchandise, except as herein provided.(1969 Code Sec.
110. 09)
876.02 LICENSE REQUIRED; FEE.
   (a)   No person shall operate a temporary store without first obtaining a
license therefor and paying a fee of one hundred fifty dollars ($150. 00). Such
license shall be issued and signed by the Mayor, upon application and upon such
forms as he may prescribe.
(1969 Code Sec. 110.06)
   (b)   No person shall refuse or neglect to pay the license fee required by
subsection (a) hereof within forty-eight hours after demand therefor, except as
otherwise provided in this chapter.
(1969 Code Sec. 110.11)
876.03 BOND REQUIRED.
   The Tax Commissioner, upon issuance of a license to operate a temporary
store, shall immediately demand payment of the license fee therefor or, in lieu
thereof, shall require the owner or operator thereof to furnish, or cause to be
furnished, a good and sufficient bond in the sum of two hundred dollars ($200.
00), payable to the City, with surety satisfactory to the Tax Commissioner and
conditioned upon the continuation in business of such owner or operator at the
address indicated thereon for a period of 120 days or more after the opening of
such business. It is the intended purpose oil this section to secure for the
City full and adequate assurance that the operator of any store which may, in
fact, prove to be a temporary store shall pay directly or indirectly, through
his surety, the license fee provided in Section
876.02.
(1969 Code Sec. 110.10)
876.04 EXCEPTIONS.
   The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any person selling by
sample only or selling agricultural products or articles of his own manufacture
or production; to any sale pursuant to the order of any court of competent
jurisdiction in the State; or to any person owning or operating a branch store,
provided that such person, or the principal of such person, has been engaged in
the same kind of business in the City for a period of more than 120 days prior
to the date of opening such branch store.
(1969 Code Sec. 110.08)
876.99 PENALTY.
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: See Section
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.)
CHAPTER 878
Video Service Provider Fee
878.01   Establishment; calculation.
878.02   Payment on quarterly basis.
878.03   Mayor to provide notice to service providers.
878.01 ESTABLISHMENT; CALCULATION.
   There is hereby established a Video Service Provider (VSP) Fee to be
calculated by applying the VSP Fee percentage of three percent to the video
service provider’s gross revenues as defined in Ohio R.C. 1332.32(B). For
purpose of calculating the VSP fee, the provider’s gross revenues shall include
advertising revenues in accordance with Section 1332.32(B)(2)(g) of the Video
Law and the Video Law gross revenues definition as established herein shall
apply equally to all video service providers and cable television operators
providing video services in the City.
(Ord. 10-29. Passed 9-7-10; Ord. 10-32. Passed 10-18-10.)
878.02 PAYMENT ON QUARTERLY BASIS.
   The VSP Fee shall be paid by any and all video service providers providing
service in the City on a quarterly basis but not sooner than forty-five days
nor later than sixty days after the end of each calendar quarter pursuant to
Ohio R.C. 1332.32(A).
(Ord. 10-29. Passed 9-7-10.)
878.03 MAYOR TO PROVIDE NOTICE TO SERVICE PROVIDERS.
   The Mayor is hereby authorized and directed to provide any video service
provider with notice of the VSP Fee percentage, including the provision that
provider gross revenues are to include advertising revenues as established
herein, which notice shall be given by certified mail, upon receipt of notice
from any such video service provider that it will begin providing video service
in the City pursuant to a state-issued video service authorization.
(Ord. 10-29. Passed 9-7-10; Ord. 10-32. Passed 10-18-10.)
CHAPTER 880
Weights and Measures

880.14
880.01 STANDARDS.
   The standards of weights and measures adopted by the State shall be the
standards of the City. The City shall procure from the State Director of
Agriculture and maintain the necessary and approved standards with their
subdivisions for the purpose of testing and approving the weights and measures
to be used in the City.
(1969 Code; Sec. 97. 01)
880.02 CITY SEALER OF WEIGHTS AND MEASURES.
   (a)   Appointment. The Mayor shall appoint, subject to the confirmation of
Council, a City Sealer of Weights and Measures who shall hold office for the
term of two years next succeeding the date of his appointment and until his
successor is duly appointed and qualified.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 02)
   (b)   Meaning of "City Sealer." As used in this chapter "City Sealer" means
the City Sealer of Weights and Measures appointed pursuant to subsection (a)
hereof and any deputy or assistant of the City Sealer who is duly authorized to
perform the duties of such officer.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.16)
   (c)   Duties. It shall be the duty of the City Sealer and he is hereby
authorized and required, at least once a year, to test all weights, measures,
scales, beams, steelyards, platform scales and other machinery or appliances,
utensils or receptacles used for weighing commodities to be bought or sold
within the City at the several places where the same are used, when practical
to do so, or at his office or place of business. If he finds the same to be
correct, according to the City standards, he shall seal and mark the same
either with a stamp or seal or by pasting a card thereon, as he may deem
proper. The character of letters and figures to be stamped or sealed thereon
shall be "N. S. " meaning thereby "Newark Standard," and the date or year of
stamping or sealing.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.04)
880.03 PRODUCTION AND EXHIBITION OF WEIGHTS, ETC., FOR TESTING.
   No person, when called upon by the City Sealer of Weights and Measures,
shall fail to produce and exhibit any and all weights, measures, scales, beams,
steelyards, platform scales or other machinery or appliances, utensils or
receptacles used by them for weighing or measuring any article or commodity to
be bought or sold. No itinerant peddler, hawker or other person who has no
office, store or other regularly established place of business in the City, but
who uses a weight, measure, scale, beam, steelyard, platform scale or other
machinery or receptacle for the purpose of weighing or measuring, shall fail to
take the same to the office of the City Sealer and have the same tested and
sealed before using it and at least once in every six months thereafter.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 05)
880.04 WEIGHTS AND MEASURES OUT OF ORDER.
   All weights, scales, beams, steelyards, platform scales or other machinery
or appliances used for weighing, which are out of order, shall be labeled "out
of use" and ordered to remain out of use until repaired, when they shall again
be sealed by the City Sealer of Weights and Measures.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.06)
880.05 RECORDS AND REPORTS.
   It shall be the duty of the City Sealer of Weights and Measures to keep a
daily record of all weights, measures, scales, beams, steelyards, platform
scales or other machinery or appliances, utensils or receptacles used for
weighing or measuring, tested by him, sealed, adjusted or made to conform to
the established standards as provided in this chapter, together with the
location, name and business of the owner thereof. Such record shall be placed
on file in his office not later than 12:00 noon of the day following the date
of such report and shall at all times be subject to the inspection of the
public. The City Sealer shall report to the Mayor the names of all persons
whose weights, measures, scales, beams, steelyards, platform scales or other
machinery or appliances, utensils or receptacles, wagons or vehicles used for
measuring or weighing 'have been ascertained by him to be out of order or
incorrect and shall file with the Mayor riot later than the fifth day of each
month a detailed summary or statement of all his official transactions for the
preceding month.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.07)
880.06 TESTING, MARKING AND SEALING REQUIRED.
   No person using weights, measures, scales, beams, steelyards, platform
scales or other machinery or appliances, utensils or receptacles for weighing
or measuring any article or commodity intended to be bought or sold in the
City, or in the weight and measurement of which other persons or the public are
interested, shall fail to cause the same to be tested, marked and sealed by the
City Sealer of Weights and Measures.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 08)
880.07 WEIGHING ®R MEASURING AT TIME OF SALE.
   No person shall sell any article or commodity which is commonly sold by
weight or measure unless such article or commodity, at the time of such sale or
purchase, is first weighed or measured by weights, measures, scales, beams,
steelyards, platform scales or other machinery or appliances, utensils or
receptacles tested, marked and sealed by the City Sealer of Weights and
Measures as required by this chapter.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 09)
880.08 BOXES, BASKETS, ETC., TO BE MARKED OR, LABELED.
   No person shall sell or expose for sale any commodity or article which is
commonly bought or sold by measure, in a box, basket, package, measure, utensil
or receptacle which does not contain either the standard half bushel or some
multiple or aliquot part thereof and which is distinctly marked or labeled so
as to show the exact quantity therein contained.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 10)
880.09 ALTERING WEIGHTS OR MEASURES.
   No person, with the intent to use the same for weighing or measuring
articles or commodities to be bought or sold, shall alter or cause or permit to
be altered or knowingly use or permit to be used after the same have been
altered, any weights, measures, scales, beams, steelyards, platform scales or
other machinery or appliances, utensils or receptacles for weighing or
measuring after the same have been tested, marked and sealed as required by
this chapter, and which by reason of such alteration do not conform to the
standards established in Section
880.01.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.11)
880.10 UNAUTHORIZED MARKING ®R SEALING.
   No person shall mark or seal or cause to be marked or sealed any weight,
measure, scale, beam, steelyard, platform scale or other machinery or
appliance, utensil or receptacle which is used or intended to be used for
weighing or measuring any article or commodity to be bought or sold.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.12)
880.11 FALSE OR INACCURATE WEIGHTS ®R MEASURES.
   No person shall knowingly use or cause or keep to be used for measuring any
article or commodity to be bought or sold or offered or exposed for sale, any
measures, utensils or receptacles for measuring, which are liable to or do
indicate false or inaccurate measure or which do not conform to the standards
established in Section
880.01. In addition to the penalty provided in Section
880.99, it shall be the duty of the City Sealer of Weights and Measures to
seize all such measures, utensils or receptacles used for measuring and to
destroy the same within twenty-four hours after seizure.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.13)
880.12 OBSTRUCTING OR HINDERING SEALER.
   No person shall obstruct or hinder the City Sealer of Weights and Measures
in the performance of any of the duties imposed upon him by the provisions of
this chapter.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.14)
880.13 DUTY OF SEALER AS TO VIOLATIONS.
   It shall be the duty of the City Sealer of Weights and Measures to enter
complaint against any person who violates or causes to be violated any of the
provisions of this chapter.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.15)
880.14 OFFICE OF SEALER.
   The Director of Public Service shall provide the City Sealer of Weights and
Measures with an office where weights, measures, scales, beams, steelyards,
platform scales or other machinery or appliances, utensils or receptacles may
be brought for the purpose of being stamped, marked or sealed and the City
Sealer shall arrange his time such that he or his deputy is at such office at
least two hours of each day for such purpose.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.16)
880.15 COAL TO BE WEIGHED ON APPROVED SCALES; DELIVERY OF WEIGH BILL TO
PURCHASER.
   No person shall sell or deliver coal in the City unless such coal is first
weighed on scales approved by the State or the County or City Sealer of Weights
and Measures. A weigh bill bearing the signature of the mine weigher and the
person selling the coal shall be furnished the purchaser upon delivery thereof.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.18)
880.16 ICE; CHARGING, ETC., FOR GREATER WEIGHT THAN DELIVERED.
   (a)   No person engaged in the business of selling or delivering ice at a
stipulated price per pound or hundredweight shall charge, collect or receive or
attempt to charge, collect or receive from any person to whom any such ice has
been sold or delivered, for any greater number of pounds of ice than has been
actually delivered to such purchaser.
(1969 Code Sec. 97.19)
   (b)   No person engaged in the business of selling or delivering ice at. a
stipulated price per pound or hundredweight, on the streets of the City, shall
sell or deliver the same to any purchaser in the City without first causing the
same to be correctly weighed at the time of delivery by the person. delivering
the same. All agents and employees of any person engaged in the business of
selling or delivering ice shall be provided with the necessary scales or
weighing apparatus to enable them to correctly weigh each piece of ice
delivered at the time of delivery.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 20)
   (c)   No person engaged in the business of selling or delivering ice in the
City shall refuse, upon demand, to allow a purchaser to whom ice is being
delivered to witness the weighing of the same at the time of such delivery, or
refuse, upon demand therefor, to furnish to any such purchaser a written
statement of the actual number of pounds of ice delivered to such purchaser at
the time of such delivery.
(1969 Code Sec. 97. 21)
880.99 PENALTY.
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: See Section
804.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.)
